development.title: Chress
development.imageAlt: A screenshot of the Chress game interface.
development.description: Chress is a browser-based RPG with turn-based combat and infinite procedural worlds. It runs in browsers on desktop and mobile without installation. The codebase was developed using parallel agent management - while all art assets and music were created by hand.

caseStudy.problemStatement: This project started as a sandbox for me to explore game mechanics and AI. The challenge then became: how to build a big browser-based game with many AI agents without being buried in tech debt?
keyChallenges: Ensuring interconnectivity in procedurally generated infinite zones.
Isolating and fixing bugs from complex AI agent interactions.
Smooth HTML5 Canvas rendering on all devices
caseStudy.solutionApproach: Vite's testing strategy was essential for managing AI complexity. This allowed for isolated debugging of agent behaviors, preventing tangled code. The project also uses a modular, event-driven architecture to keep systems decoupled and scalable.
keyFeatures: Turn-Based Tactical Combat: Engage in strategic battles with 6 chess-inspired enemies. Complete Chess challenges with power-ups.
Infinite Procedural World: Endlessly generated and handcrafted world with diverse zones, from overworlds to underground dungeons.
Barter with dozens of unique NPCs, play with a complex inventory of items and equipment, and interact with a dynamic environment.
Progressive Web: Complete offline play capabilities and automatic updates.

design.title: Ochlo
design.imageAlt: A screenshot of the Ochlo application interface.
design.description: Ochlo provides secure, decentralized communication for groups that need to organize in real-time. By allowing anyone to create an instant, encrypted local network without user accounts, it's a vital tool for community action, public demonstrations, and any event where privacy and immediate coordination are paramount.

caseStudy.problemStatement: Current communication tools require account creation and centralized servers, creating privacy concerns and barriers to quick, secure communication in sensitive situations.
keyChallenges: Balancing security with ease of use
Designing for various technical skill levels
caseStudy.solutionApproach: I designed a streamlined interface that generates secure communication channels instantly, using visual metaphors that make complex security concepts accessible to all users.

design.title: Eugene Access
design.imageAlt: A screenshot of the Eugene Access application.
design.description: Our public spaces are often hostile to basic human needs. Eugene Access is my one-day design challenge to that reality. It's a zero-friction tool that provides immediate answers: Is the bathroom public? Is it clean? What's the wifi password? This is about redesigning public space to be for the public.

caseStudy.problemStatement: People in crisis situations struggle to quickly find essential services due to fragmented information sources and complex navigation systems in existing platforms.
caseStudy.designPhilosophy: Prioritized clarity and speed over visual complexity. Every element serves the core purpose: connecting people to help as quickly as possible.

design.title: Cash Cache
design.imageAlt: A screenshot of the Cash Cache income visualizer application.
design.description: I built Cash Cache on a simple premise: managing money is more motivating when you can actually see it. This wacky income visualizer turns your earnings into a dynamic animation, offering a more satisfying way to watch your finances accumulate.

caseStudy.problemStatement: Traditional financial apps present data in boring, text-heavy formats that fail to engage users or provide meaningful insights into spending patterns.
researchInsights: Visual data is processed 60x faster than text
caseStudy.visualStrategy: Created an engaging visual language using progressive data visualization that reveals insights gradually, making complex financial data approachable and actionable.
